item.title: US Supreme Court justices skeptical of Trump attempt to end birthright citizenship
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Supreme Court Wednesday seemed poised to reject the Trump administration’s attempt to redefine the constitutional right to birthright citizenship, and instead uphold the country’s long understanding of citizenship by birth on American soil. item.title: NM official calls for full environmental review of Carson National Forest uranium mine proposal
item.description: Tirzio Lopez, a board member of the Upper Chama conservation district, said a full review is necessary of Gamma Resources' Canjilon proposal.

item.title: NM state treasurer joins national call to fix economy after year of ‘Liberation Day’ tariffs
item.description: New Mexico State Treasurer Laura Montoya on Wednesday morning joined state officials across the nation to voice concerns about the economic effects in the year since President Donald Trump announced his “Liberation Day” tariffs.

item.title: New Mexico Department of Justice urges state Supreme Court to stop Otero County ICE contract
item.description: Attorney General Torrez argued that Otero County lacks authority to hold federal immigrant detainees who have not been charged or convicted.

item.title: NM Supreme Court upholds judge’s decision to toss challenge to Duke Rodriguez gubernatorial campaign
item.description: Justices on the New Mexico Supreme Court on Wednesday afternoon unanimously upheld a District Court judge’s decision to dismiss a challenge to the legitimacy of former state cabinet secretary Duke Rodriguez’s Republican campaign for governor.

item.title: New Mexico officials, tribes accuse feds of rushing efforts to reverse Chaco Canyon drilling ban
item.description: The Trump administration, for the last year, has floated a proposal to reverse a Biden-era order that issued a 20-year ban on oil and gas development on federal lands within 10 miles of the site, which holds paramount spiritual and cultural significance for numerous tribes and pueblos.

item.title: New Mexico Republicans seek legislative committee on fraud, waste, abuse
item.description: Every Republican in the New Mexico state Senate on Tuesday co-signed a letter requesting an interim legislative committee focused on vetting allegations of fraud, waste and abuse in state government.
